Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How weight is calculated

Convert mass to gravitational force using W = m × g, with an editable gravitational acceleration. The default is standard Earth gravity; this is a force estimate and should not be confused with everyday scale readings that often display mass units. A 10 kg mass weighs about 98.1 newtons at standard gravity. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Weight is a force, and the SI unit of force is the newton. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

weight force = mass × gravitational acceleration
A worked example

A 10 kg mass weighs about 98.1 newtons at standard gravity.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why does weight use newtons?

Weight is a force, and the SI unit of force is the newton.

Can I use this on another planet?

Yes. Enter an appropriate local gravitational acceleration, if known.
